indicators.note: something convertible can be changed into another form, so the letters of the next word are rearranged

explanation.surface: An open-topped Italian car is described as a piece of someone's property.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Convertible' looks like a car, but it signals that the letters of ROMAN are rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: A manor is a landed estate, a kind of real property.

clue.text: The painter has to shake it up

indicators.note: in a down clue, up means the pieces are read from bottom to top, backwards

parts.note: to toss is to shake or jerk about
taken as written

explanation.surface: An artist is told he must give something a good shake.
explanation.walkthrough: 'up' turns TOSS IT round as a whole, giving the name of James Tissot, the French painter of Victorian society scenes.
explanation.definitionFit: James Tissot was a nineteenth-century French artist who worked in London.

clue.text: Force acquiring thousands by way of business

indicators.note: one word acquiring another takes it inside itself

parts.note: to coerce is to force someone
M is the Roman numeral for a thousand, doubled for the plural

explanation.surface: Pressure brings in big sums as a means of doing trade.
explanation.definitionFit: Commerce is trade, the buying and selling that makes up business.

clue.text: Bill will be paid for this

definitions.text: Bill will be paid for this

parts.words: Bill will be paid for this
parts.note: read as a person called Bill being rewarded, but really a document handed over once an invoice is settled

explanation.surface: Someone called Bill can expect payment for his work.
explanation.definitionFit: A written acknowledgement of payment is handed over when an account is settled.

indicators.note: a reproduction is a copy made anew, here a rearranged version of the furniture maker's name

explanation.surface: A copy of a Sheraton piece of furniture is on board a ship at sea.
explanation.walkthrough: Sheraton is a style of eighteenth-century English furniture; 'the main' is an old poetic term for the open sea.
explanation.definitionFit: The main is a poetic name for the ocean, and this is a particular sea off Britain's east coast.

clue.text: People are not fit to be given them

definitions.text: People are not fit to be given them

parts.words: People are not fit to be given them
parts.note: read as a judgement of unworthiness, but 'not fit' means unwell, so these are what sick people receive

explanation.surface: Some things should be kept from those who do not deserve them.
explanation.definitionFit: Drugs and remedies are prescribed to people who are ill, that is, not fit.

indicators.note: something happening unexpectedly comes out in a surprising order, so the letters are mixed

explanation.surface: Some vocalists surprise everyone by nodding off and snoring.
explanation.definitionFit: Male voices pitched between tenor and bass belong to these vocalists.

explanation.surface: Something is called tidy, yet second-rate.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Neat' is the old word for cattle; a cow is something that lows, or moos.
explanation.definitionFit: Cattle low, or moo, so a cow is one that lows; and a lesser grade is lower.

parts.note: F is forte, the musical direction for loud
an air is a tune

explanation.surface: Someone describes a piece of music as rather noisy.
explanation.definitionFit: Fair in its old sense means beautiful or attractive.

parts.note: to con is to study or learn by heart
the Somme is a river in northern France

explanation.surface: Someone researches the route a river takes.
explanation.definitionFit: A clear soup is served as one course of a meal.

clue.text: She'll set a good man free

parts.note: ST, short for saint, is a good man
to rid is to free or clear

explanation.surface: A woman intends to release a virtuous fellow.
explanation.walkthrough: 'She' points to a woman's name; the 'll and 'set' only join the pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: A girl's name, Scandinavian in origin, so a woman fits the pronoun.

explanation.surface: Advice to get going once the weather cools down.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cooler' is slang for prison, as is the other sense here.
explanation.definitionFit: To stir is to move or budge; stir and cooler are both slang for jail.

clue.text: Drinks are of some help in this place

parts.note: port is a fortified wine, so ports are drinks
aid means help

explanation.surface: A traveller notes that a glass or two helps in a certain town.
explanation.definitionFit: A city in Egypt at the northern end of the Suez Canal is the place meant.

parts.note: a bay is a horse with a reddish-brown coat
a diner who leaves food does not eat it

explanation.surface: A chestnut-coloured horse turns its nose up at the herbs in its feed.
explanation.definitionFit: The aromatic foliage of the laurel tree is used as a cooking herb.

indicators.note: repairing puts something back together, here the word's letters in a new order

explanation.surface: A tradesman is described as someone who fixes ladders.
explanation.walkthrough: 'who repairs' reads as part of the job description but rearranges LADDERS.
explanation.definitionFit: A leather worker who makes and mends horse tack is this craftsman.

clue.text: Little Sidney turned the lock, causing much trouble

indicators.note: turned means the short name is read backwards

parts.note: Sid is a short form of Sidney
a tress is a lock of hair

explanation.surface: A young man called Sidney turns a key and causes great upset.
explanation.definitionFit: Great anguish or hardship is grave trouble.

clue.text: Show animal taken around totally unadorned

indicators.note: the first piece is taken around the second, holding it inside

parts.note: a cat is an animal
bare means wholly without decoration

explanation.surface: A performing creature is paraded around stark naked.
explanation.definitionFit: A nightclub entertainment of song and dance is a kind of show.

clue.text: A graduate register may be reduced

parts.note: BA, Bachelor of Arts, is a graduate
a table is a list or register

explanation.surface: A student's name on the list might be cut.
explanation.definitionFit: Something that can be lessened or abated is open to reduction.

indicators.note: letters that go wrong are put in a disordered arrangement

explanation.surface: Getting old brings torments that feel quite unjust.
explanation.definitionFit: Intense pains or torments are sufferings.

clue.text: Make a song about the whip cutting

indicators.note: the first piece goes about, or around, the second

parts.note: to sing is to make a song
a lash is a whip

explanation.surface: Someone complains noisily about a flogging.
explanation.definitionFit: Slashing criticism is severe and hurtful, cutting in tone.

indicators.note: some of the following word is used, a run of its inner letters

explanation.surface: A small island is praised as unusually lovely.
explanation.definitionFit: A small Hebridean island off Mull, known for its abbey, is the isle meant.

parts.note: the gar is a fish with a long snout

explanation.surface: A choice is offered between something from the sea and a seaweed extract.
explanation.definitionFit: A jelly made from red algae is used in cooking and laboratories.

parts.note: as means like, in the manner of
read as the plural groups; sets are groups

explanation.surface: Something resembles the holdings of a collective.
explanation.definitionFit: Valuable property and holdings count as resources.

parts.note: C stands for circa, Latin for about

indicators.note: brought round means the word is read backwards

parts.note: to peer is to look closely

explanation.surface: Someone crawls about, glancing back over their shoulder.
explanation.definitionFit: To move slowly with the body close to the ground is to crawl.

clue.text: Serving men in a store can appear quite useless

indicators.note: one piece is placed in the other

parts.note: a barn is a farm building for storing crops
RE is the Royal Engineers, men serving in the British Army

explanation.surface: Soldiers stuck in a storehouse look idle and pointless.
explanation.definitionFit: Barren means unproductive, yielding no result.

parts.note: read as a nasty old vessel, but beastly means full of beasts, the animals of the Flood story

explanation.surface: Someone sneers at a horrid old tub.
explanation.definitionFit: In Genesis, the vessel carried the animals two by two through the Flood.

indicators.note: the word may be turned into another by rearranging its letters

explanation.surface: A gardener says the hedges may be pruned.
explanation.walkthrough: 'clipped' looks like the gardening verb but defines a short, curt manner.
explanation.definitionFit: Clipped speech is brief and abrupt, the same as curt.

clue.text: Important communication from the Soviet bloc?

parts.note: Red was a common term for the communist Soviet bloc
a letter is a written communication

explanation.surface: A message arrives from behind the Iron Curtain.
explanation.definitionFit: Saints' days were printed in red in church calendars, so a memorable day is special.
